elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b): "The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to..." — the cap runs to both IBM and MSL; the pre-existing mutuality was retained.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) caps at "the fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" only; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, add "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 15.3(a): "Neither Party will be liable to the other for lost profits, consequential, punitive, or incidental damages" — bilateral; "indirect" is not expressly named but consequential/incidental damages are excluded on both sides.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c): "The limitation in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party's ... breach of its confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in Section 15.
New 15.3(c): "does not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations", which lifts MSL's 15.1 indemnity out of the cap.
New 15.3(c) expressly excludes "gross negligence" from the 15.3(b) limitation.
New 15.3(c) expressly excludes "willful misconduct" from the 15.3(b) limitation.
Fraud is absent from the new 15.3(c) carve-out list; add "fraud" to the excluded claims to reach preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in rendered 15.3(c); only the indemnification obligations are excluded, which does not expressly cover direct infringement claims of the other party's IP.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in rendered 15.3 states that IBM's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to the cap; no such sentence was added.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) applies "for either Party", and no residual language leaves IBM's liability unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.3(b) now reads "limited to the fees paid or payable by IBM under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", replacing the 3%-of-bill-of-materials basis.
New 15.3(c): "The limitation in Subsection 15.3(b) does not apply to a Party's indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New 15.3(c) carves out "breach of its confidentiality obligations", placing the Section 13.2 duties outside the cap.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: the cap remains mutual, is re-based on twelve months of fees paid or payable by IBM, and the single new subsection (c) supplies exactly the four fallback carve-outs (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct).

Preferred is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP, and no statement that IBM's payment obligations are outside the capped damages.

Minimality holds: only the cap basis in 15.3(b) was replaced and one carve-out sentence added; the favourable mutual consequential/punitive/incidental waiver in 15.3(a) and the mutual framing of (b) are retained, and no survival tails, expense language, or extra damages categories were bolted on.

Intent preserved: the cross-reference in new (c) points correctly to Subsection 15.3(b); the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement $25,000 limit and the Section 15.1 indemnity mechanics are untouched and not contradicted.

Drafting caveat (not a defect): "fees" is lower-case and undefined in this manufacturing/outsourcing context where IBM pays Product prices; consider "amounts paid or payable by IBM for Products and Services" if MSL argues purchase prices are not "fees".

Optional uplift toward preferred in negotiation: append "fraud", "breach of data protection or security obligations" and "infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" to 15.3(c), and add the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor.
